title: From chaos to flow: how AI helps us prototype faster in Unity
author: Golovan2
selftext:
During prototyping, bugs in Unity can seriously slow down the whole process not just for one dev, but for the entire team. Deadlines slip, sprints fall apart, burnout creeps in.

We started using an AI assistant that plugs into the project and fixes bugs on the fly. It doesn’t just scan stack traces it actually understands the project context: code, assets, plugins, dependencies, settings, and more. As a result, we spend less time digging through code and more time focusing on gameplay and design.

Some of the biggest improvements we’ve seen:

* Faster prototyping, with almost no delays in iteration
* Tech debt isn’t piling up like it used to
* Easier to test ideas early in the dev cycle
* Sprints are more predictable, with fewer late-night crunches

It’s not just a code generator it’s more like a co-pilot that genuinely understands what’s going on in the project. Sometimes it catches things we wouldn’t have noticed until way later.

If anyone’s curious, I can share a quick demo video. It’s become a solid part of our pipeline

replies.author: Golovan2
replies.body: Thank you! We are trying very hard!

comments.author: OkThereBro
comments.body:
Is this actually faster? Like, the example you gave would've been faster for me to fix than your ai to. Without doubt. Especially such a small, blatant issue, that's a beginner "bug" if ive ever seen one. 

Can it fix complex issues? Things theres not information online for?

At the moment it serves as a decently competent middle man. But that's still a middle man, and it isn't demonstrating anything actually useful to someone with experience.

replies.author: Golovan2
replies.body:
You are partly right, especially about the role of a “mediator.” I wouldn't call it a mediator, it's an assistant.

An experienced developer can indeed handle a simple task faster, especially in a familiar context. But in practice, even a minor edit takes time: you need to understand the structure of the project, figure out the dependencies, and remember the nuances. And over time, it only gets more complicated.

CM is not a silver bullet or a replacement for a developer. But as an assistant that removes routine tasks, helps navigate the code, explains details, and highlights potential risks, it is indeed useful.
